data.title: Tom Lee says Ethereum is bottoming – A whale is betting $45M that he’s right
data.description:
Volatility often goes hand in hand with speculation, and Ethereum is a clear example of this.

The past 48 hours have been a rollercoaster for the altcoin. According to CoinGlass, nearly $300 million in long positions have been wiped out.

However, this still does not compare to the liquidity squeeze seen earlier in October, which saw almost $500 million of positions liquidated as ETH broke below the $2.5k support level, triggering a 7% correction.

This time, despite erasing nearly $300 million worth of long positions, ETH has corrected by just over 1%. This suggests that selling pressure remains relatively contained, at least for now. Could this mean Tom Lee was right to say Ethereum is close to bottoming out?

As can be seen in the post above, a trader who claims to have a perfect 100% win rate has opened up another long trade on Ethereum. The trader had used 25x leverage to go long on 20,277 ETH for an investment of $45.3 million.

This trade has already resulted in $252,000 of profit. The interesting part is that the trader’s  previous 10 trades have all been profitable, resulting in $6.32 million in realized gains.

Given this track record and the fact that ETH has had limited downside despite heavy futures selling, this could be an interesting sign.

It could suggest that the trader is positioning ahead of a potential recovery that the broader market has yet to price in, adding another bullish angle to Tom Lee’s $2k ETH bottom thesis.

That said, the real test may still be ahead.

Ethereum’s bottom call faces a test as supply outpaces demand 

The market is still not fully convinced that Ethereum [ETH] has found its bottom.

For starters, on-chain data suggests that uncertainty is also showing up in staking demand, which continues to weaken. According to ValidatorQueue, there are about 1,036,882 ETH (over $2.3 billion) waiting to go into the Ethereum mainnet validator queue.

This is a considerable drop compared to 3,737,802 ETH six months ago, suggesting fewer investors are looking to lock up their ETH for staking rewards.

Meanwhile, institutional sentiment remains negative. Over the past five weeks, there have been continuous outflows from Ethereum ETFs, with $270 million in net outflows already recorded in less than a week since November began.

If this trend continues, November could see outflows exceed October’s $1.6 billion, putting further pressure on ETH and its recovery prospects.

Unless these factors start to improve, calling an Ethereum bottom could be premature.

For now, ETH remains exposed to further downside. Long positions are building despite fading technicals, weakening interest in staking demand, and increased ETF outflows.

On top of this, a large long-liquidation cluster exists below $2200 ETH. If overall sentiment remains weak, ETH could sweep this liquidity, potentially falling below the $2k level before a potential reversal.

This suggests that the market may need another round of downside before Tom Lee’s bottom thesis gets stronger support.

Final Summary

data.title: Why aren’t XLM crypto traders betting big before the 23 November vote?
data.description:
Stellar’s [XLM] next upgrade just cleared its testnet vote. Validators will decide on the mainnet version in a couple of weeks.

Hence, the question – Has the token’s price moved in lockstep?

Stellar’s Bell upgrade passes testnet

Bell (also known as Protocol 30), cleared its testnet vote on 3rd November. Validators will vote on the mainnet version on the 23rd.

According to the Stellar Development Foundation, Bell would bring three changes. The first will involve letting smart contract tell payments for different customers apart. This would make life immensely easier for businesses.

The second change will allow smart contracts check post-quantum signatures as the network’s own signatures would stay the same. The last would switch ledger timing to milliseconds. Here, it’s worth noting that they’ve admitted that this change along won’t make blocks faster.

Also, 23rd is not the final launch date. In fact, Bell only goes live if validators approve it, with the Foundation clarifying that the date could still move.

In the meantime, wallets, exchanges and node operators need to update their software.

XLM crypto falls ahead of the vote

Ideally, an upgrade would put the price up on its shoulders. Not this one though.

XLM went up to about $0.171 on the 4th, then came tumbling down the next afternoon. It’s been stuck between $0.153 and $0.157 since. At press time, it was valued at around $0.155.

Indicators seemed to be indecisive. The RSI was at 45.2, under the Signal Line. The ADX on the DMI was at around 18.5. What did this indicate? Well, there didn’t seem to be a strong trend either way, though sellers were just slightly ahead.

Futures traders have mostly taken a few steps back too. Open interest dropped from about $94 million to $88 million during the slide and at the time of writing, it was $89.5 million. Funding was barely positive at 0.0011% too.

Simply put, it may be evident that everyone’s playing it safe. No one’s betting big before the big 23rd November vote. For now, $0.16 is the level to watch.

Final Summary

  • Stellar’s Bell upgrade passed the testnet vote.
  • Validators are set to make a mainnet decision on the 23rd.

data.title: Is crypto’s 2026 outlook at risk as regulatory FUD returns to Washington?
data.description:
After the election, investors are looking for clues about crypto’s regulatory future.

However, one thing is clear: the road ahead remains uncertain, with volatility already creeping into the market. The impact of the recent election goes beyond the broader U.S. macro environment, extending into the regulatory landscape as well. The crypto industry has seen huge gains under Republican leadership in the U.S. with President Donald Trump’s vision of making the country the “crypto capital of the world.”

However, with Republicans holding a narrow majority in Congress, investors are becoming more cautious about what comes next. The recent challenges faced with the CLARITY Act, and the increased focus from the SEC around tokenizations, are adding to the uncertainty in the regulatory outlook.

That said, signs of a regulatory shift are already starting to emerge.

In the latest development, House Democrats are drafting a new bill regarding how crypto should be structured moving forward. The bill includes expanding the SEC’s jurisdiction and will also include provisions excluded from the CLARITY Act. This comes ahead of any potential change in who controls Congress.

From a regulatory standpoint, tighter SEC oversight could mean stricter compliance rules, increased scrutiny of crypto firms, and greater regulatory pressure on digital asset companies operating in the U.S. The key takeaway? Regulatory pressure may not stop at tighter SEC oversight.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, known to be a strong crypto critic, is expected to become the Chair of the Senate Banking Committee, potentially giving her greater influence over financial regulation and crypto policy.

Bitcoin risks deeper losses amid rising regulatory uncertainty

Is regulatory FUD shaping up to be the next major bearish catalyst for the broader crypto market?

The recent political upheaval in the U.S. Congress has already started to affect regulation. Discussions around a new crypto market structure bill, increasing anti-crypto sentiment and potential increased scrutiny from the SEC are adding a new layer of uncertainty to an already volatile market.

Further adding to the concern, Bitcoin [BTC] is looking bleak on its yearly chart. Historically, Bitcoin has never closed consecutive years in the red. However, this could change soon. Bitcoin is currently trading around 12% lower on its 2026 yearly candle, with just two months left before the year closes. This follows a red candle in 2025, putting BTC at risk of recording its first-ever back-to-back years of annual losses.

In essence, Bitcoin’s next move may depend on more than just market sentiment.

As regulatory uncertainty increases amid potential increased attention from the SEC, Bitcoin has another factor to contend with. If selling pressure continues, BTC could be heading toward its first-ever back-to-back annual losses, breaking a decade-long historical trend.

Final Summary

data.title: XRP bear trap alert! Bitfinex shorts surge 652% as supply tightens
data.description:
The current market breakdown could go either way. 

On one hand, this can lead to a further capitulation phase for the market as key support levels come under threat. However, it could also be seen as a bear trap for those short sellers who have stretched their positions too far. Notably, XRP seems to be at the forefront of this debate.

As the chart below shows, Bitfinex XRP shorts have spiked by 652.89% to 468.2 million. Given the weakening technical momentum, this bearish positioning is not entirely surprising. The altcoin has seen five straight  weekly lows and broken below the $1.20 support level, with its price now approaching the $1 mark.

Meanwhile, XRP’s relative strength is adding another layer of pressure. 

After breaking out of its five-week consolidation, the XRP/ETH pair has dropped over 3% this week. This indicates that XRP is losing value to Ethereum, as traders are showing preference towards ETH in this current bear trend. This relative weakness in XRP is therefore contributing to the bearish sentiment.

From a technical standpoint, betting on more Ripple [XRP] downside, with $1 as the next target, looks like a calculated move rather than a random bet. However, on-chain signals are telling a different story, keeping the possibility of a bear trap on the table.

XRP supply shock signals challenge bearish bets 

XRP is flashing textbook signs of a potential supply shock.

On the 5th of September, an estimated 13.24 million XRP was taken off exchanges, limiting the amount available to sell (as noted by one analyst). Moreover, whale holdings have increased by nearly 60 million XRP over the past week. While it is unclear whether these are the same tokens that left exchanges, both signals point to growing accumulation by large holders. 

The key takeaway? XRP’s Binance Scarcity Index has hit its highest level since 2022. As shown in the chart below, the index has been deeply negative throughout September and October before making a sharp move higher in recent days. The index is now extremely positive, and it is one of its largest movements in almost 4 years. This indicates that XRP supply is becoming tighter on Binance.

Ultimately, XRP is showing a clear split between its technical and on-chain signals. 

While negative momentum and increasing short interest indicate that there is more downside to come, market outflows, whale accumulation, and reduced Binance supply suggest that selling pressure may be losing steam. If these supply patterns remain, then those shorting the market hoping for a fall to $1 may be caught off guard, turning the current bearish setup into a potential bear trap. 

Final Summary

data.title: ‘Worst days in history’ – Trump’s stock-market reaction meets crypto’s $900B slide
data.description:
Bloodbath is the perfect word to describe the post-election market action.

Despite the markets trading on the assumption that Democrats will win, with odds hitting a high of 99%, crypto has suffered a severe sell-off. However, the downside may not be over yet. The total crypto market cap has now slipped back to mid-September levels, marking five straight weeks of losses and wiping out nearly $900 billion in market value.

The result? A textbook liquidity sweep. According to Coinglass, nearly $1 billion in positions were liquidated on the 5th of September, marking the largest single-day wipeout since the $2 billion short squeeze in mid-August. However, unlike that event, nearly 80% of the liquidations came from longs, showing that bullish traders were heavily caught offside as the market moved lower.

That said, the sell-off wasn’t just “crypto-specific.”

As the chart above shows, the Nasdaq 100 suffered its largest one-day loss since the pandemic, while the S&P500 lost $3 trillion in value. This comes just 24 hours after the Dow surged 1,600 points after Democrats swept the midterms. This indicates that there has been an abrupt change in sentiment post-election.

Notably, the U.S. President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to say that it is one of the stock market’s “worst days in history.” The crypto wipeout seems to be part of a wider correction in the market, with post-election volatility adding to the selling pressure. However, the move may not be just another election-driven pullback. The latest market data suggests there could be more going on beneath the surface.

Crypto faces fresh capitulation risks as market sentiment weakens

The market FUD seems to be less about the election itself and more about President Trump.

From a technical standpoint, this shift in sentiment makes sense. Crypto initially saw a strong boost from optimism around his election, but that momentum has since faded. However, the momentum has died out. Bitcoin [BTC] is currently down almost 30% from its peak of $126k despite progress made in regulation with the GENIUS Act, greater tokenization and increased adoption in stablecoins into traditional finance.

To add to the pressure, there are now reports that Trump Media sold a total of $343 million worth of Bitcoin. This adds to concerns regarding institutional selling and has also created more FUD around Trump, further weakening the bullish sentiment that initially drove crypto’s post-election rally.

Against this backdrop, crypto’s wipeout could be more than just a reaction to broader market weakness.

Besides the traditional markets digesting how the election will affect the AI space, there are further pressures on the crypto space. On top of reports that Trump Media is selling off its Bitcoin, there continue to be outflows from ETFs. In essence, crypto is facing its own market-specific headwinds.

In turn, crypto could be entering a more severe capitulation phase now that prices have retreated back to mid-September levels.

Final Summary

data.title: Chainlink price prediction: How LINK can avoid a breakdown below $8
data.description:
Many of the large-cap crypto assets were deep in the red amid intense selling pressure in the past 24 hours. Chainlink [LINK] was one of the assets with the most bearish sentiment in the speculative markets.

At the time of writing, the Open Interest (OI) fell 11.6% in 24 hours alongside a 7.3% price slump as the The Funding Rates also retreated toward zero but were still positive.

The past month’s liquidation heatmap revealed a notable magnetic zone at $12 and another just under $13. These clusters of liquidity could attract LINK prices higher in the short term before a move lower.

In related news, Chainlink expanded access to Asian stock markets. This tokenization push has not bred new demand for the altcoin.

Examining Chainlink’s higher timeframe movement

The weekly chart revealed a swing level at $15 that the altcoin swept in September before falling lower. Another swing point at $10.87 was on the verge of being broken.

A weekly session close below this level would suggest a move toward $7.88, and $7 could be the next multi-week price leg.

As the liquidation heatmap showed, there was a smattering of liquidity around $10.30, which had a confluence with a recent weekly low of $10.27. Hence, a bullish short-term scenario would be a price sweep of $10.27 followed by a bounce past $11.80.

Chainlink bulls unable to overcome trendline resistance

For weeks now, Chainlink has seen a steady bearish trend sustained on the 4-hour timeframe. In particular, the month-long trendline resistance (orange) was a formidable opponent for buyers.

Additionally, it could be decision time for LINK. The $10.61 swing low from mid-September was under increasing pressure from the sellers, evidenced by the lower lows in recent weeks. Moreover, something has to give, and it is likely to be the buyers’ resolve.

Final Summary

  • Chainlink saw an 11.6% slide in Open Interest and a 7.3% price decline in 24 hours, making its short-term outlook among the most bearish in the top crypto assets.
  • The repeated challenge of the $10.6-$10.8 zone and steady selling pressure meant LINK could be headed towards $7.88 in the coming weeks.

data.title: Cardano Node 11.2 brings Dijkstra closer, but why did its price fall by 6%?
data.description:
Cardano [ADA] has an update coming soon. 

Node 11.2 is expected to hit mainnet by 8th November, and it will bring Dijkstra features with it.

Usually, a big release would give the price something to work with. Not this time though.

Cardano Node 11.2 pre-release lands, Leios saved for 11.3

Cardano Node 11.2 is out… only as a pre-release for now. The GitHub notes say it isn’t recommended for mainnet yet. The full release, likely tagged 11.2.1, is expected by the weekend (8th November).

The biggest change isn’t quite obvious though.

Node configs now come in a new “envelope” format; nodes older than 11.2 won’t be able to read them. Basically, this means operators will have to upgrade. The node’s API also got a boost. It can now run over a network address instead of only locally, and it picked up new tools for checking the mempool.

On the Dijkstra side, the CLI now handles sub-transactions. Dijkstra transactions can be submitted through the API too.

Leios is only groundwork here, and it’s switched off by default. The real thing is planned for Node 11.3, which is already being built.

Fair Min Fees will have to wait too.

Cardano dropped by 6.7% in a day, but…

… a $0.19 liquidity cluster is right above it.

The sell-off involved ADA falling from about $0.199 on 5th November to a low near $0.178 overnight.

The altcoin eventually clawed its way back to $0.186. However, at press time, it was still 6.7% below where it began.

The RSI on the short-term chart was at 48.3 too.

Additionally, the leverage has also taken multiple hits. Open Interest went down from about $197 million to $181 during the drop.

Funding seemed to be positive too with a reading of 0.0057%. This implied that longs haven’t given up yet.

Here’s what’s interesting, though. There appeared to be big pile of liquidations stacked on the heatmap, between $0.188 and $0.19. These seemed to be just above the press time trading price.

Prices cam often drift toward spots like that.

If Cardano pushes into that zone, those shorts could get squeezed… fast.

Final Summary

  • Cardano Node 11.2 is out as a pre-release; full mainnet release expected by weekend.
  • ADA fell by about 6.7%, with a liquidation cluster just above the price at press time.

data.title: Core Scientific plans to shut down Bitcoin mining despite Q3 revenue hitting $233M
data.description:
Core Scientific, once the largest Bitcoin [BTC] miner, has released its Q3 2026 report, but at the same time it has also announced its plans to completely exit Bitcoin mining by the end of 2026.

During its Q3 2026 earnings call, Chief Financial Officer Jim Nygaard said the company expects to complete the mining wind-down in the fourth quarter and enter 2027 as a high-density colocation provider.

This decision came as the firm’s Q3 results were primarily driven by the expansion of its high-density colocation (HDC) business, which supports AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads.

Core Scientific’s AI shift

Remarking on the same, CEO Adam Sullivan said,

We are nearing full delivery under our first colocation agreement while construction under our second is underway across five campuses.

According to the reports, the company’s colocation revenue surged nearly 60% quarter-over-quarter to $215.4 million, compared to $136.7 million in Q2 2026 and $15 million in Q3 2025.

In fact, its total revenue also increased to $232.9 million, up from $164.2 million in the previous quarter and $81.1 million a year earlier.

As of the 30th of September, Core Scientific was billing for 485 megawatts (MW) of capacity, up from 395 MW in the previous quarter, representing more than $700 million in average annualized colocation revenue.

Core Scientific’s Q3 2026 results

That said, the company also reported net income of $1.178 billion, compared to a net loss of $1.15 billion in Q2 2026 and $144 million in Q3 2025.

Meanwhile, adjusted EBITDA more than tripled quarter-over-quarter to $133.6 million, with its margin expanding to 57% from 25% in the previous quarter. Core Scientific’s gross profit also climbed to $123.3 million, compared to $70 million in Q2.

However, on the mining side, self-mining revenue declined to $12.3 million from $21.5 million in the previous quarter, while hosted mining revenue stood at $5.17 million. At the same time, revenue from hosting equipment for other Bitcoin miners also declined to $5.2 million from $8.7 million.

How it all began?

For those unaware, Core Scientific began its AI infrastructure transition in 2024 through hosting agreements with CoreWeave, covering 590 MW of capacity, of which 485 MW was billable by September 2026. However, the transition also comes with challenges.

Core Scientific recorded $266.5 million in mining-related asset impairments in Q1 2026 amid weaker Bitcoin prices, low mining profitability, and declining equipment values. It also recorded a $41.9 million loss after terminating mining equipment agreements with Block and Proto in Q2.

That said, Core Scientific is not the only one, as, according to AMBCrypto’s recent report, Bitcoin miners are increasingly selling BTC to fund operations while shifting their infrastructure towards AI and HPC.

Miner’s November performance analysis

This comes as miners swung from a huge inflow spike of about +7K BTC  in early 2026 to an outflow of about -5.7K BTC in early November, while the price slid from around $95K to $75.5K.

However, the latest netflow has settled back to a small positive reading of about 179.4 BTC, which suggests the miner selling pressure has cooled.

Final Summary

  • Q3 results were primarily driven by the expansion of its high-density colocation (HDC) business.
  • Core Scientific began its AI infrastructure transition in 2024 through hosting agreements with CoreWeave.

data.title: Hyperliquid Strategies posts $620.6M Q3 profit – Mostly unrealized HYPE gains
data.description:
Hyperliquid Strategies Inc., the largest publicly traded HYPE treasury company, announced that its subsidiary has applied for registration as a US futures commission merchant (FCM).

CEO David Schamis said,

We deployed $802 million this quarter and filed an application to become a futures commission merchant. Those two moves are the same bet.

Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. reports quarterly financials

Hyperliquid was dominant in the part of on-chain finance that delivers real fees, and this value flows back to HYPE holders through systematic buybacks, the CEO added.

The company reported $620.6 million in quarterly profits. However, $803 million in unrealized gains came from its HYPE holdings, which totaled 38.9 million, with an average cost of $56.35 per token.

It raised $911 million in equity capital for the quarter ending on the 30th of September, spending $785 million to acquire 9.1 million HYPE tokens.

An FCM is a registered intermediary that holds customer funds and handles futures orders. The subsidiary would serve permissioned markets under HIP-3*, a planned upgrade whose regulatory approvals are pending.

If approved, Hyperliquid would get a regulated entry point for U.S. traders in the same week. There is no guaranteed timeline for the HIP-3*’s approval, the company stated.

Right now, the company’s stock, PURR, is highly correlated to HYPE token price swings.

Whales sell after billionaire Hyperliquid tweet pushes HYPE to local highs

On the 29th of October, billionaire American investor Stan Druckenmiller tweeted about Hyperliquid. Santiment Intelligence reported that this pushed the token price to local highs of $97.

Whale wallets were steadily selling their holdings during the rally. Four whales closed their longs entirely, banking around $5 million. The largest of these dumped $225k every five minutes when the price was around $95 and short-term sentiment was euphoric.

The weekly bullish structure extended from $51.13 to $97.99 (orange). The daily structure was also bullish, but the $75.17 swing low from September has been challenged once already.

The recent retreat from $97 revealed the sellers’ strength. A deeper drawdown below $75.17 remains likely. In that case, swing traders and investors should watch the $60.50-$68.35 demand zone.

Final Summary

  • The largest HYPE treasury company reported a $620.6 million profit for the latest completed quarter, mostly due to unrealized gains on HYPE holdings.
  • A subsidiary’s FCM application would serve permissioned markets under HIP-3*, which the company pitched to shareholders as regulated U.S. trader access to perpetual futures.

data.title: Bitcoin reclaims $80K – Why THESE signals threaten BTC’s price recovery
data.description:
Bitcoin [BTC] has reclaimed the $80,000 level, which is sitting above the 100-week Exponential Moving Average (EMA). This indicates a potential shift from short bearish control to bullish as long as BTC remains above the EMA.

The broader market is also green, with gains of about 2.38% on the day, with the total crypto capitalization approaching $2.70 trillion.

On the charts, Bitcoin is trading above a bull flag that had been in place since late September 2025. The EMA is also trading above the 0.50 Fibonacci retracement levels, a confirmation that BTC is entering the premium zone.

Still, buyers have yet to show real dominance over bears with the MACD faintly green.

Therefore, a breakdown to around $60,000 may be viable if bulls cannot keep the price above the EMA. The $60,000 level is aligned to 0.618 Fibonacci, a zone where most assets tend to bounce from.

Conversely, if bulls manage to sustain the strength, BTC could equal its all-time high of $126K, though $90,000 remains a significant supply zone. However, BTC is facing conflicting signals when on-chain data is explored.

Miner transfers and ETF outflows test buyer strength

Bitcoin miner, MARA Holdings, seems to be selling their Bitcoin holdings once again. The mining firm has moved 1,650 BTC worth over $132 million to Galaxy Digital, Copper, and other platforms.

Basically, Galaxy Digital received around 698 BTC valued at $56 million, while other platforms shared the remaining bounty from the Coinbase custody.

At the same time, U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs continued to see capital outflows over this week. For instance, in the past 24 hours, investors sold over $115 million in ETFs. This result took the weekly outflows to $990.98 million, less than $10 million away from hitting $1 billion.

This capital outflow from institutions puts bulls under a critical test of whether they can withstand this selling pressure.

The only way Bitcoin can hold its recovery above $80,000 is if buyers continue to long the token. At the same time, the selling pressure from the aforementioned institutions needs to stay in check, not outweighing the buyers’ volume.

Therefore, holding on to the new structure will be dependent on the behavior of market participants, including retailers, large investors, and institutions.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin reclaimed the $80,000 level, flipping the 100-week EMA into support, an indication of a potential shift to a long-term bullish structure. 
  • BTC was turning bullish on the weekly chart, but MARA’s dumping and Bitcoin ETF outflows tested its buyer strength.
